commands.strataindustria.oil.none: No oil reservoir under this chunk
commands.strataindustria.oil.reservoir: %s reservoir centred at %s, %s: top at Y %s, %s%% left, %s seeps
commands.strataindustria.oil.seep: Seep at %s, %s: %s blocks of crude oil
death.attack.strataindustria.hot_item: %1$s held on to hot metal for too long
death.attack.strataindustria.hot_item.pl: %1$s held on to hot metal for too long while fighting %2$s
heat.strataindustria.too_hot: Too hot to hold bare-handed. Tongs in your off hand would help.
item.strataindustria.bell.hint: Hangs from the underside of a block. Right-click to ring.
item.strataindustria.fume_hood.hint: Set it directly above a crucible. Arsenic fumes rise while the pot is poured.
item.strataindustria.ledger.charcoal_bur: Third burn this month. Sealed it with turf this time and it came out black all the way through. Last one was half ash.
Out of straw. Walked to the next clearing for more, two days there and back. Leaving the axe here, the handle is split anyway.
item.strataindustria.ledger.collapsed_ad: Roof came down Tuesday. Nobody hurt. The props at the far end still hold, we think. Not going back in.
Followed the vein from the portal and it dips. Props every three steps. Bring plenty of timber.
Lower level flooded again. Pumps can't keep up. Moving the crew to the east face.
Poor ore at the edges. Nothing in the middle but hard grey stone we can't cut. Foreman says leave it. Pay day Friday.
item.strataindustria.ledger.placer_worki: River gravel, three pans a day. Gold is heavy and sits at the bottom. Tip slow and the light stuff goes over the edge.
Water rose and took half the trough. Will rebuild when it drops.
item.strataindustria.ledger.prospector_c: Three stones on the counter, top rock, middle rock, bottom rock, in that order. Every hill here stacks them the same way. Look at the stones before you dig. Spare things are in the crate at the end of the trench.
Tin stone half a day out. Needs a copper pick and mine is stone. Marked the spot, will come back.
item.strataindustria.ledger.ruined_bloom: Fire bricks crack after a few burns. The pale clay holds longest. Stack lost three, spares are in the crate. Slag is mostly iron still, don't throw it out.
Bloom came out small again. Too little charcoal, too much hurry. Don't open it before the glow is gone.
Stack plan. Pale bricks only, three to a side, the door on the front and the chimney on top. Slag collects at the bottom.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.b: Showing where the hill is cut.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.c: Heavy dark pebbles in the stream.
Black stone. Needs a better pick.
Showing where the hill is cut.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.g: Showing where the hill is cut.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.h: Red, heavy. Too hard for our picks.
Red streak. Bronze barely marks it.
Red all over. Needs a harder pick.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.l: Showing where the hill is cut.
Brown ore in wet ground. Use a shovel.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.m: Heavy black, drags a knife blade.
Green rubs off on the fingers.
Under the soil. Stone picks do.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.n: Near the grass. Stone picks do.
Gold in white rock. Too soft for tools.
Gold in the river sand below.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.s: Showing where the hill is cut.
Showing where the hill is cut.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.hand.t: Harder metal than the green ore.
item.strataindustria.survey_notes.unread: Not read yet. Hold them a moment.
item.strataindustria.tongs.tooltip: In the off hand: hold hot metal without burns
journal.strataindustria.observe.boiler_d: Engine ran dry halfway. Need a water stop.
journal.strataindustria.observe.clay: Clay squeezes between my fingers and keeps the shape. Fired, it might hold water. Or metal.
journal.strataindustria.observe.coal: Black stone that burns. Too dirty for iron as it is, but baked in a closed oven it might come out clean.
journal.strataindustria.observe.copper_n: A green-stained pebble with a bead of raw copper in it. If I could get it hot enough to run, I could cast it.
journal.strataindustria.observe.flint: Flint breaks with an edge sharper than any rock. Worth knapping.
journal.strataindustria.observe.gold_nug: A fleck of gold. Pretty and soft, and no good for tools.
journal.strataindustria.observe.hungry_p: Pony stopped at the stop. No hay left.
journal.strataindustria.observe.iron_nug: A rust-red pebble, heavy for its size. No crucible fire of mine will touch this; iron wants a furnace of its own.
journal.strataindustria.observe.link.cop: Copper again, and the same little blue flower over it. I think they go together.
journal.strataindustria.observe.link.hor: Gold in the gravel, and horsetail on the bank above it.
journal.strataindustria.observe.link.pin: Tin under the pink flowers. Same as the last time.
journal.strataindustria.observe.link.stu: Zinc and lead under the yellow birches. Whatever is in that ground stunts the trees.
journal.strataindustria.observe.overstre: The shaft groaned and stopped. I asked more of it than its power can give; fewer machines, or more power.
journal.strataindustria.observe.plant.co: A small blue flower, a kind of mint, growing in a patch on this hill. I have not seen it on the other hills.
journal.strataindustria.observe.plant.ho: Jointed grey stalks with a ring of thin needles at every joint, standing in a clump on the bank.
journal.strataindustria.observe.plant.lo: Violet flower spikes on bare granite. Nothing else grows close to them. I don't know what they are telling me.
journal.strataindustria.observe.plant.pi: Pink pompoms on a mat of grass, in soil too thin for most things.
journal.strataindustria.observe.plant.st: A birch that stopped at knee height. Its leaves have gone yellow, and so has every other one around it.
journal.strataindustria.observe.raw_hide: A raw hide. It already smells; left like this it will rot. Something must stop that.
journal.strataindustria.observe.survey_n: Someone's field notes on an ore deposit.
journal.strataindustria.observe.tin_nugg: Heavy dark grains, unlike copper. The old smiths said a little of something like this, melted into copper, makes a harder metal.
journal.strataindustria.observe.too_hard: The %s is too hard for the pick in my hand. %s
journal.strataindustria.place.cabinet.hi: Every rock of one kind, or every mineral, in a specimen cabinet. My pick reaches further into rock I know.
journal.strataindustria.place.charcoal_b: Someone stacked logs here, buried them under earth and never lit them. A pile sealed on every side burns slowly into charcoal instead of ash. Cover the open side with earth, then light it. They slept warm. Look where they slept.
journal.strataindustria.place.collapsed_: The mouth of an old mine has fallen in. Mine timbers still hold up the tunnel beyond. Old tunnels were dug toward ore.
journal.strataindustria.place.mining_cam: Miners followed this vein into the hill, propping the tunnel as they went. They stopped at the poor ore on the vein's edge; the rich ore at the heart of a vein is still down there. Their notes mention ore their picks could not cut.
journal.strataindustria.place.placer_wor: Panners washed river gravel here and left a heap they never finished. Heavy grains settle when gravel is swirled in water; the light stuff washes away. Look for glints in river gravel. They hid what they found where the river could watch it.
journal.strataindustria.place.prospector: A prospector laid three stones on a counter: the rock at the surface, the rock below it, and the hard rock at the bottom. Every region stacks its own three rocks, and every rock keeps its own ores. The pebbles of ore on the ground here sit above a vein. The trench ends where they stopped digging.
journal.strataindustria.place.ruined_blo: A chimney of pale bricks, cracked by heat, and heaps of glassy slag. Smiths once made iron here: not by melting it, but by baking ore with charcoal in a tall brick stack. These bricks were made from a special pale clay. The slag still holds a little iron. Three bricks are missing from the stack. The roof fell on something. Move the beams.
Four different minerals on one specimen shelf. Cut samples turn up in old camps, adits and caches.
journal.strataindustria.root.hint: Every goal of the field journal at a glance. Switch this tab on in the config to open it from the journal.
journal.strataindustria.study.bloomery.b: The %s roars. The bloom is growing inside.
journal.strataindustria.study.bloomery.c: The %s is charged and waiting for a flame.
journal.strataindustria.study.bloomery.e: The %s stands empty. It wants iron ore and charcoal.
journal.strataindustria.study.bloomery.i: The %s is not finished. Fire bricks all round, a chimney, and open air above it.
journal.strataindustria.study.bloomery.n: The %s has ore but not enough charcoal to bake it.
journal.strataindustria.study.bloomery.r: The %s has burned down. The bloom is ready to pull out.
journal.strataindustria.study.bloomery.t: The %s will not get hot enough. More air would make it roar; a bellows, perhaps, or a taller chimney.
journal.strataindustria.study.boiler.dry: The %s is firing dry! Water, now, before it is ruined.
journal.strataindustria.study.boiler.hea: The %s ticks and creaks as the water heats.
journal.strataindustria.study.boiler.low: The %s is running low on water.
journal.strataindustria.study.boiler.no_: The %s is cold. It needs a burning firebox under it.
The %s is dry. Firing it empty would ruin it; it needs water first.
journal.strataindustria.study.boiler.pip: The pipe on the %s cannot take steam this hot. It needs a stronger pipe.
journal.strataindustria.study.boiler.too: The %s is warm but will not boil. The fire under it needs to be hotter.
journal.strataindustria.study.boiler.ven: The %s is venting: more steam than anything is using.
journal.strataindustria.study.lead: I looked the %s over closely. It has something to do with a question I have been asking.
journal.strataindustria.study.plain: I looked the %s over closely. Nothing I did not already know.
journal.strataindustria.study.plant.copp: %s. It grows in patches, and only on some hills. Worth looking under.
journal.strataindustria.study.plant.hors: %s. Likes wet gravel. It takes up more from the ground than most plants.
journal.strataindustria.study.plant.loco: %s. Cattle that eat it go strange. It must be taking something from the rock.
journal.strataindustria.study.plant.pink: %s. It grows where the soil is thin and the rock is not far below.
journal.strataindustria.study.plant.stun: %s. Something in the ground is poisoning it.
journal.strataindustria.study.rock: %s, a %s rock. Veins in it tend to hold %s.
journal.strataindustria.study.rock.barre: %s, a %s rock. I have never heard of ore in it.
journal.strataindustria.t0.clay.hint: Gather five clay balls. Look along riverbanks and in swamps.
journal.strataindustria.t0.clay.lead: The banks of the river are slick and grey. Is that clay?
journal.strataindustria.t0.clay.note: Wet clay, a good armful of it. It holds whatever shape I press into it.
journal.strataindustria.t0.crafting_tabl: I keep working on my knees in the dirt. A bench would help.
A flat top and four legs. Everything is easier with a place to work.
journal.strataindustria.t0.fire.hint: Build a fire pit from sticks and straw, put fuel in, and hold a firestarter on it.
journal.strataindustria.t0.fire.lead: The nights are cold and the meat is raw. How do I make fire?
journal.strataindustria.t0.fire.note: Smoke, then a glow, then flame. I sat by it a long while.
journal.strataindustria.t0.knap.hint: Hold two loose rocks or one flint, use it, and strike away the waste until a tool head is left.
journal.strataindustria.t0.knap.lead: If I strike one rock against another, could I chip out an edge?
journal.strataindustria.t0.knap.note: Flake by flake, a rough head came free. Sharp enough to cut, if I am careful. Limestone and shale crumble; rhyolite and flint flake clean.
journal.strataindustria.t0.log.hint: Fell a tree with your axe. Bare hands will not do.
journal.strataindustria.t0.log.lead: The trees here would give me timber, if I had a way to fell them.
journal.strataindustria.t0.log.note: The trunk came down with a crack that echoed through the woods.
journal.strataindustria.t0.loose_rock.hi: Pick up a loose rock lying on the ground.
journal.strataindustria.t0.loose_rock.le: Bare hands won't get me far. Is there anything lying around I could use?
journal.strataindustria.t0.loose_rock.no: A fist-sized rock, picked off the ground. It is a start.
journal.strataindustria.t0.stone_axe.hin: Bind a knapped axe head to a stick with twine.
journal.strataindustria.t0.stone_axe.lea: A blade is no good without something to hold it by. How do I haft it?
journal.strataindustria.t0.stone_axe.not: Lashed to a stick, the head bites into wood. My first real tool.
journal.strataindustria.t0.twine.hint: Cut grass with a knapped knife blade for plant fibre, then twist two fibres into twine.
journal.strataindustria.t0.twine.lead: Grass stems are tough when they dry. Could I twist them into cord?
journal.strataindustria.t0.twine.note: Two strands twisted against each other hold far more than either alone.
journal.strataindustria.t1.charcoal.hint: Sneak and place logs into a pile, light it, cover every face with soil or stone, then dig out the charcoal.
journal.strataindustria.t1.charcoal.lead: Wood burns too fast and too cool for real work. Can I make a better fuel?
journal.strataindustria.t1.charcoal.note: Smothered under earth, the wood charred black and light. It burns hot and clean.
Form something from clay: use five clay balls to open the forming grid.
Clay takes any shape I give it. What should I shape first?
Pinched and smoothed into a pot. Raw clay crumbles, though; it needs fire.
journal.strataindustria.t1.crucible.hint: Fire a crucible and an ingot mold in the pit kiln.
journal.strataindustria.t1.crucible.lead: If I could melt this ore, what would I pour it into?
journal.strataindustria.t1.crucible.note: A crucible to melt in and a mold to pour into, both fired hard.
journal.strataindustria.t1.forge.hint: Build a forge. It burns charcoal far hotter than a fire pit.
journal.strataindustria.t1.forge.lead: Charcoal on an open fire throws its heat away. I need something to hold it in.
journal.strataindustria.t1.forge.note: A stone hearth with walls around the coals. It glows hotter than anything I have built.
journal.strataindustria.t1.nugget.hint: Find a small ore on the surface. A vein lies somewhere below it.
journal.strataindustria.t1.nugget.lead: Some of the pebbles here are strangely coloured. What are they?
journal.strataindustria.t1.nugget.note: Ore, washed up from a vein below. Somewhere under my feet there is more.
journal.strataindustria.t1.pit_kiln.hint: Sneak and place unfired clay on the floor of a one-block pit, add 8 straw and 8 logs, then light it and let it burn out.
journal.strataindustria.t1.pit_kiln.lead: A campfire only cracks raw clay. How do I fire it evenly?
journal.strataindustria.t1.pit_kiln.note: Buried in straw and logs, the pots baked all night. They ring now when I tap them.
journal.strataindustria.t2.alloy_metal.h: Mine cassiterite, bismuthinite or tennantite ore.
journal.strataindustria.t2.alloy_metal.l: Copper bends too easily. Is there another ore that would harden it?
journal.strataindustria.t2.alloy_metal.n: Dark, heavy ore that copper alone could never be. This may be what I was missing.
journal.strataindustria.t2.brick_kiln.hi: Build a brick kiln out of bricks, set it on a lit forge, and fire clay pieces in it.
journal.strataindustria.t2.brick_kiln.le: A pit kiln takes a night and a pile of logs for a few pots. Is there a quicker way?
journal.strataindustria.t2.brick_kiln.no: A small brick oven that stands on the forge. A load of pots is done in half a minute.
journal.strataindustria.t2.bright_strike: Finish a piece without letting the metal dull. Strike while it glows, and go back to the forge when it fades.
The metal glows brightest just out of the forge. What if I never let it dull?
Every blow landed on bright metal. The piece came out finer than any I had made.
journal.strataindustria.t2.bronze.hint: Melt copper with tin, bismuth or arsenic in the right shares and cast a bronze ingot.
journal.strataindustria.t2.bronze.lead: What happens if I melt copper together with this new metal?
journal.strataindustria.t2.bronze.note: Copper and tin ran together into something golden and much harder: bronze.
Build a bronze anvil, the last tool of the bronze age.
Stone anvils crack under heavy work. Could I cast one from bronze?
A bronze anvil, solid and true. The bronze age is behind me.
journal.strataindustria.t2.bronze_armour: Wear a full set of bronze armour.
Bronze plate would turn a blow that would cut through leather.
Clad head to foot in bronze. Heavy, but I feel far safer.
Own a bronze pickaxe, axe, shovel, knife, hammer, saw and sword.
Bronze holds an edge. Every tool I own could be better for it.
Pick, axe, shovel, knife, hammer, saw and sword, all in bronze. A proper kit.
journal.strataindustria.t2.casting_table: Lay fired molds on a casting table beside a crucible and pour. One pour fills every empty mold. Click the table to knock the castings out.
I pour one mold at a time and stand and wait. Can I do several at once?
Four molds on a stone table, and one pour fills the lot.
Pour molten copper into an ingot mold and knock the ingot out once it cools.
The melt is ready. What do I do with it before it sets?
Poured, cooled, and knocked out of the mold: a bar of copper.
journal.strataindustria.t2.copper_pickax: Make a copper pickaxe. It breaks ore a stone pick cannot.
Some rock just shrugs off my stone pick. Would metal cut it?
The copper pick bites where stone only skated. New ground opens up.
journal.strataindustria.t2.handcart.hint: Pull a handcart 200 blocks without letting go of the shafts.
journal.strataindustria.t2.handcart.lead: A pack won't carry ore for long. What if the load had wheels?
journal.strataindustria.t2.handcart.note: Two wheels and two shafts. Holds a lot, but a full block stops it.
journal.strataindustria.t2.melt.hint: Set a crucible on top of a lit forge and melt ore in it.
journal.strataindustria.t2.melt.lead: Will my forge get hot enough to melt ore in the crucible?
journal.strataindustria.t2.melt.note: The ore slumped and ran. I watched a pool of molten metal shine back at me.
journal.strataindustria.t2.pack_frame.hi: Wear a pack frame in the chest slot.
journal.strataindustria.t2.pack_frame.le: My pockets are full again. What carries more than a back can hold in its hands?
journal.strataindustria.t2.pack_frame.no: Frame on my back, nine more slots. When it is more than half full I can't run.
journal.strataindustria.t2.pattern_casti: Cut a plank blank from planks and carve it on the grid into a pattern. Press the pattern into a sand flask (right-click with a flask in your pack) to get a sand mold. A sand mold takes any metal, once.
Every mold I make by hand is a day of clay. Can I carve the shape once and use it again?
A plank carved to the shape, pressed into damp sand. The sand mold takes one pour and goes, the plank stays.
journal.strataindustria.t2.prospectors_p: Strike rock with a prospector's pick to learn what ore lies nearby.
Ore hides in the rock. Could I hear it if I tapped the stone?
The rock rings differently near ore. I am learning to listen.
journal.strataindustria.t2.quern.hint: Knap a quernstone from four loose rocks and stack two under a stick for a quern. Put ore in and keep turning it; crushed ore melts down to more metal.
journal.strataindustria.t2.quern.lead: Lumps of ore melt down poorly. Would they melt better ground fine?
journal.strataindustria.t2.quern.note: Two stones turned against each other, and the ore comes out as grit. More metal from less ore.
journal.strataindustria.t2.smith.hint: Heat an ingot in the forge and lay it on an anvil. Sneak and use a hammer to pick a shape, then strike.
journal.strataindustria.t2.smith.lead: Can I beat hot metal into a shape a mold cannot give?
journal.strataindustria.t2.smith.note: Heat, strike, heat again. The ingot spread into a thin, even plate.
journal.strataindustria.t2.stone_anvil.h: Sneak and strike the top of raw igneous rock with a hammer to dress it into an anvil.
journal.strataindustria.t2.stone_anvil.l: Cast metal is brittle and rough. I need something solid to hammer it on.
journal.strataindustria.t2.stone_anvil.n: A block of hard rock dressed flat on top. It will take a beating.
journal.strataindustria.t2.trail.hint: Set four cairns or blazes in a row, each within 64 blocks of the last.
journal.strataindustria.t2.trail.lead: I will never find that tin hill again. How did the old prospectors mark a way?
journal.strataindustria.t2.trail.note: Cairns on open ground, blazes on trees. Touch one and it points to the next.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bellows.hint: Turn a bellows with a shaft and point its nozzle into a forge or a bloomery wall.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bellows.lead: Fires burn hotter with more air. Could an axle blow it in for me?
journal.strataindustria.t3.bellows.note: The bellows breathe in time with the shaft, and the coals roar white.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bloom.hint: Charge the bloomery with iron ore and charcoal, light it, and wait for the bloom.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bloom.lead: The bloomery stands ready. What do I feed it, and how long does it burn?
journal.strataindustria.t3.bloom.note: Out of the ashes came a spongy, smoking lump. Iron, full of slag.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bloomery.hint: A bloomery is a chimney of fire bricks with a door in front. Two levels are enough to start.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bloomery.lead: Iron will not run like copper. How did the old smiths ever get it out of the rock?
journal.strataindustria.t3.bloomery.note: A brick chimney with a door at the bottom. They baked the iron out instead of melting it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bucket.hint: Wrought iron is finally enough for a bucket.
journal.strataindustria.t3.bucket.lead: I have always carried water in clay. Could iron hold more?
journal.strataindustria.t3.bucket.note: A bucket of thin iron. Water, lava, anything goes where I carry it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.charter.hint: A charter post holds an outpost once a line runs to it. Lay track to it and send a tub through.
journal.strataindustria.t3.charter.lead: The tin is a long walk off. Could I keep a mine going out there?
journal.strataindustria.t3.charter.note: Charter set at the tin workings. The line runs; the place keeps working while I'm home.
journal.strataindustria.t3.core_sample.h: Turn a core sampler and press Drill to read the ground 64 blocks down.
journal.strataindustria.t3.core_sample.l: My prospector's pick only hears so far. What lies deep below?
journal.strataindustria.t3.core_sample.n: The core came up in bands: every layer of rock beneath me, laid out in order.
journal.strataindustria.t3.fire_brick.hi: Form fire clay into bricks and fire them in a pit kiln.
journal.strataindustria.t3.fire_brick.le: Fire clay is no use as a lump. What shape would let me build with it?
journal.strataindustria.t3.fire_brick.no: Fired bricks, pale and hard. Enough of these would make a furnace.
journal.strataindustria.t3.fire_clay.hin: Bronze cannot melt iron. You will need a bloomery, and it is built of fire bricks. Dig fire clay from the pale beds near the surface in shale and slate.
journal.strataindustria.t3.fire_clay.lea: Bronze cannot melt iron. What could stand a fire hotter than any I have made?
journal.strataindustria.t3.fire_clay.not: A pale, gritty clay that does not slump in the fire. Bricks of this would last.
journal.strataindustria.t3.furnace.hint: Eight fire bricks make a furnace.
journal.strataindustria.t3.furnace.lead: A furnace of fire bricks would hold its heat like the bloomery does.
journal.strataindustria.t3.furnace.note: Eight bricks and a door. It cooks and bakes without minding.
journal.strataindustria.t3.hide.hint: Animals give raw hides now. Leather has to be tanned.
journal.strataindustria.t3.hide.lead: The animals I hunt could give me more than meat.
journal.strataindustria.t3.hide.note: A raw hide, stiff and smelly. It will rot unless I treat it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.incline.hint: A winch at the top of a slope hauls tubs up on its rope. Turn it with a shaft.
journal.strataindustria.t3.incline.lead: The pony won't take that hill.
journal.strataindustria.t3.incline.note: Winch at the top, rope to the tub. Shaft turning, it climbs. Shaft stopped, it stays put.
journal.strataindustria.t3.iron_anvil.hi: Build a wrought iron anvil from double ingots. It can work steel later on.
journal.strataindustria.t3.iron_anvil.le: My bronze anvil dents under iron. Could I build one from iron itself?
journal.strataindustria.t3.iron_anvil.no: A wrought iron anvil, heavy as the earth. It will work anything I can heat.
journal.strataindustria.t3.iron_ore.hint: Iron hides in shale and slate, under swamps, and deep in dark igneous rock. Your prospector's pick can find it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.iron_ore.lead: The rust-red stone is everywhere in the old stories. Where does iron ore hide?
journal.strataindustria.t3.iron_ore.note: Red and heavy, and it took a bronze pick to cut it. Iron ore at last.
Smith a wrought iron pickaxe head and fit it to a handle.
Iron is tougher than bronze. What would an iron pick cut?
An iron pick. Rock that laughed at bronze gives way to it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.leather.hint: Soak hides in lye, scrape them with a knife, then soak them in tannin in a sealed barrel.
journal.strataindustria.t3.leather.lead: A raw hide rots. How do I turn it into leather that lasts?
journal.strataindustria.t3.leather.note: Limed, scraped and soaked in tannin for days. Supple leather, finally.
journal.strataindustria.t3.millstone.hin: Drive a millstone from an axle and let it grind for you.
journal.strataindustria.t3.millstone.lea: My arms ache from the quern. Could the axle grind for me?
journal.strataindustria.t3.millstone.not: The millstone grinds day and night, and I never have to touch it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.pattern.hint: Pick a shape on the anvil, then sneak and use a blank pattern on it. A hammer machine will work that shape.
journal.strataindustria.t3.pattern.lead: I smith the same pieces again and again. Could the anvil remember a shape for a machine?
journal.strataindustria.t3.pattern.note: The shape is marked on a blank pattern. A machine can work it now.
journal.strataindustria.t3.pony.hint: A harness puts a horse on the rails. It wants hay at the stops.
journal.strataindustria.t3.pony.lead: Pushing tubs this far is no good.
journal.strataindustria.t3.pony.note: Put the old horse on the tramway. Two trips a bale.
journal.strataindustria.t3.refine.hint: Hammer a hot bloom on a bronze anvil to squeeze out the slag.
journal.strataindustria.t3.refine.lead: The bloom is full of slag. How do I get clean iron out of it?
journal.strataindustria.t3.refine.note: Hammered hot, the slag squirted out in sparks. What is left is wrought iron.
journal.strataindustria.t3.rotation.hint: Put a hand crank on the end of a wooden axle and hold right-click on it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.rotation.lead: Every machine I can picture needs something turning. Where does the turning come from?
journal.strataindustria.t3.rotation.note: A crank on an axle, and my arm makes it turn. Slow, but a start.
journal.strataindustria.t3.saw_mill.hint: Fit a saw blade to a saw mill and saw a log: six planks and the bark.
journal.strataindustria.t3.saw_mill.lead: Splitting planks by hand is slow and wasteful. Could a turning blade do better?
journal.strataindustria.t3.saw_mill.note: The saw mill rips a log into planks in moments, with the bark left over.
journal.strataindustria.t3.tramway.hint: Set a tub on wooden rail between two tub stops and let it roll in. Stops hold it until their rule lets it go.
journal.strataindustria.t3.tramway.lead: A handcart is no good on a long haul. What if the load rode on rails?
journal.strataindustria.t3.tramway.note: Plank rails and a tub on wheels. Slow, and it stops short if I don't push, but it keeps to the line.
journal.strataindustria.t3.trip_hammer.h: Put a hot raw bloom in a trip hammer, or give it a recorded pattern and a forge beside its anvil.
journal.strataindustria.t3.trip_hammer.l: With a pattern and a turning shaft, could a hammer work by itself?
journal.strataindustria.t3.trip_hammer.n: The trip hammer rises and falls on its own, following my pattern blow for blow.
journal.strataindustria.t3.wash.hint: Scoop placer gravel from a river bed with a washing pan and swirl it standing in water.
journal.strataindustria.t3.wash.lead: There is ore in the river gravel. Could I wash it out?
journal.strataindustria.t3.wash.note: Swirled in the pan, the light gravel washed away. Heavy grains stayed behind.
journal.strataindustria.t3.water_power.h: Set a water wheel on an axle where flowing water pushes one side of it.
journal.strataindustria.t3.water_power.l: The river never stops running. Could it turn my axles for me?
journal.strataindustria.t3.water_power.n: The wheel caught the current and has not stopped turning since.
journal.strataindustria.t3.weld.hint: Heat two iron ingots, lay both on the anvil and strike them together into a double ingot. No flux needed.
journal.strataindustria.t3.weld.lead: One ingot is too small for the bigger tools. Could two be joined while hot?
journal.strataindustria.t3.weld.note: Hammered together white hot, two ingots became one. The seam does not show.
journal.strataindustria.t4.automated_cha: Let a machine finish 64 items in a row with everything arriving and leaving by belt, chute, inserter or hopper, and nobody opening it.
I spend my days carrying ore from one machine to the next. Could the machines pass it along themselves?
Belts, chutes and inserters, and a crusher that ran through a whole load with nobody there to feed it.
journal.strataindustria.t4.blast_furnace: Build a five-high refractory furnace, blow air into its tuyere and charge it with iron ore, coke and flux. Tap the pig iron.
Crucibles melt iron a little at a time. Could a whole tower of it run at once?
Air roaring into the tuyere, and pig iron running out of the tap hole.
journal.strataindustria.t4.boiler.hint: Set a bronze boiler on a burning firebox, fill it with water and wait for the needle to rise.
journal.strataindustria.t4.boiler.lead: Water swells into steam when it boils. Could I trap that force?
journal.strataindustria.t4.boiler.note: A bronze boiler over a firebox, and the gauge needle climbing.
journal.strataindustria.t4.brass.hint: Melt calcine with copper and a little carbon dust. Two parts copper to one of zinc.
journal.strataindustria.t4.brass.lead: What would copper and zinc make together?
journal.strataindustria.t4.brass.note: Brass, bright as gold and easy to work. Fine fittings will come from this.
journal.strataindustria.t4.coal.hint: Coal lies in deep shale and arkose seams. Bronze will not cut it.
journal.strataindustria.t4.coal.lead: Charcoal costs a forest. Is there black rock that burns?
journal.strataindustria.t4.coal.note: Coal, cut from a deep seam. It burns long and hot, but smoky.
journal.strataindustria.t4.coke.hint: Bake coal in the coke oven. Coke burns hot enough to melt steel.
journal.strataindustria.t4.coke.lead: The oven is ready. What comes out of coal baked without air?
journal.strataindustria.t4.coke.note: Grey, light coke that burns hotter than any fuel I have had.
journal.strataindustria.t4.coke_oven.hin: Fire coke oven bricks and build a hollow 3x3x3 oven with a door in the middle of one side.
journal.strataindustria.t4.coke_oven.lea: Raw coal is too dirty for iron. Could I bake the dirt out of it?
journal.strataindustria.t4.coke_oven.not: A sealed oven of brick, hollow inside. Whatever I put in will bake without air.
journal.strataindustria.t4.converter.hin: Blow air through pig iron in a converter, with a coke to preheat it. Watch the flame: when it drops, the steel is done.
journal.strataindustria.t4.converter.lea: Pig iron is brittle from all its carbon. Could I blow the carbon out of it?
journal.strataindustria.t4.converter.not: Air through molten pig iron, a roaring flame, and when it died down: steel by the ton.
journal.strataindustria.t4.creosote.hint: Draw the creosote from the oven into a bucket and treat planks with it.
journal.strataindustria.t4.creosote.lead: The oven drips a thick black oil. Is it good for anything?
journal.strataindustria.t4.creosote.note: Creosote. Planks soaked in it shrug off rot and water.
journal.strataindustria.t4.crusher.hint: Drive a crusher at 16 RPM or more. Ore comes out crushed, sometimes with a second piece and a bit of another mineral.
journal.strataindustria.t4.crusher.lead: Steam is strong enough to crush rock. Could it break ore finer than a millstone?
journal.strataindustria.t4.crusher.note: The crusher eats ore and spits out grit, often with a little extra besides.
Lay four or more heat pipes from a burning firebox to a boiler or a heat inlet. Copper pipe holds the heat down to 1000 °C.
Every machine burns its own fire. Could one fire feed them all through pipes?
Heat ran down the pipe from the firebox and warmed a boiler two rooms away.
journal.strataindustria.t4.locomotive.hi: Coal in the firebox door, water in the tank. Give it a couple of minutes and it comes up to pressure.
journal.strataindustria.t4.locomotive.le: A pony and wooden rail won't do for the long haul.
journal.strataindustria.t4.locomotive.no: Engine's up to full pressure. Whistle works.
journal.strataindustria.t4.molten_iron.h: Melt iron in a refractory crucible on a forge burning coke, with bellows.
journal.strataindustria.t4.molten_iron.l: Could iron be melted outright, with coke and enough air?
journal.strataindustria.t4.molten_iron.n: Iron ran liquid in the crucible. I never thought I would see it.
journal.strataindustria.t4.outpost_5.hin: A locomotive run over steel track the whole way, between two charters, gives the outpost more ground.
journal.strataindustria.t4.outpost_5.lea: Wooden rail keeps the place small.
journal.strataindustria.t4.outpost_5.not: Steel track all the way. The outpost loads wider now.
journal.strataindustria.t4.pipe.hint: Join copper plates with solder into pipe. Copper carries a bronze boiler's steam.
journal.strataindustria.t4.pipe.lead: Steam and water need a way to get from one place to another.
journal.strataindustria.t4.pipe.note: Plates soldered into pipe. Now I can carry fluids wherever I need them.
journal.strataindustria.t4.railway.hint: Station track at each end, a water tower and a coal stage at home. Take the brake off with an empty hand and sneak, and leave it. Three round trips.
journal.strataindustria.t4.railway.lead: Can't sit on this engine all day.
journal.strataindustria.t4.railway.note: Runs by itself. Water and coal at home, that's all it wants.
journal.strataindustria.t4.refractory_cr: Form a crucible from fire clay and fire it. It stands the heat of melting iron.
My old crucible would crack in a fire hot enough for iron. What would stand it?
A crucible of fire clay, fired hard. It will hold molten iron.
journal.strataindustria.t4.roast.hint: Zinc ore must be roasted before it will melt. A hot forge will do.
journal.strataindustria.t4.roast.lead: Zinc ore stinks of sulfur and will not melt clean. How do I drive the sulfur off?
journal.strataindustria.t4.roast.note: Roasted in the forge until the fumes stopped, the ore turned to a crumbly calcine.
journal.strataindustria.t4.solder.hint: Galena melts like tin ore. Alloy its lead with tin.
journal.strataindustria.t4.solder.lead: How do I join metal without welding it white hot?
journal.strataindustria.t4.solder.note: Lead and tin melt low and hold fast. Solder joins what heat cannot.
journal.strataindustria.t4.sphalerite.hi: Find sphalerite. Zinc is the key to brass.
journal.strataindustria.t4.sphalerite.le: Copper and tin make bronze. Is there an ore that makes something brighter?
journal.strataindustria.t4.sphalerite.no: Sphalerite, glittering and brown. The smiths called it blende: zinc ore.
Pipe a boiler's steam into the back of a steam engine. At 2 bar it turns a shaft at 32 RPM.
Steam pushes hard. Could it turn a shaft faster than any river?
The engine hisses and the shaft spins. Steam power at last.
Give a steam hammer a recorded pattern, steam at the back and heat from below, and let it smith steel.
A pattern replays my hand's work. Could steam swing the hammer and keep the iron hot as well?
The steam hammer thunders away at steel and never lets it cool. A hundred plates without lifting a hand.
journal.strataindustria.t4.steel.hint: Stir coke or charcoal dust into molten iron, one dust to five ingots, and cast it in a refractory mold.
journal.strataindustria.t4.steel.lead: Iron is tough but soft. Would a little carbon make it hard?
journal.strataindustria.t4.steel.note: A pinch of carbon stirred into molten iron, and it set as steel.
journal.strataindustria.t4.steel_anvil.h: Weld steel into double ingots and build an anvil that can work anything.
journal.strataindustria.t4.steel_anvil.l: Steel is too hard for my iron anvil. What will work it?
journal.strataindustria.t4.steel_anvil.n: A steel anvil. There is no metal left that it cannot shape.
journal.strataindustria.t5.alumina.hint: Mix clay and sulfuric acid into alum, then roast it in an electric furnace or a roaster.
journal.strataindustria.t5.alumina.lead: Clay is mostly one metal that fire alone cannot free. What else could pull it out?
journal.strataindustria.t5.alumina.note: White powder, alumina, and sulfur gas going up the vent.
journal.strataindustria.t5.aluminium.hin: Electrolyse alumina with a coke dust. It takes a long run and a lot of power.
journal.strataindustria.t5.aluminium.lea: Alumina will not melt out like other ores. Could the wire drag the metal out?
journal.strataindustria.t5.aluminium.not: A silver ingot, light as wood. Aluminium.
journal.strataindustria.t5.assembler.hin: Load an assembler with the parts of one of its recipes and let it run.
journal.strataindustria.t5.assembler.lea: Small parts take me a day by hand. Could a machine put them together?
journal.strataindustria.t5.assembler.not: The assembler fitted six parts together on its own.
journal.strataindustria.t5.battery.hint: Charge a battery box to half. Dynamos and generators fill it when nothing else needs power.
journal.strataindustria.t5.battery.lead: A dynamo makes power only while the shaft turns. Can I keep some?
journal.strataindustria.t5.battery.note: Half full and holding. It will run a machine when the shaft stops.
journal.strataindustria.t5.cable.hint: Place an LV cable against a dynamo or a machine. Cables join on their own.
journal.strataindustria.t5.cable.lead: Power in the dynamo is no use there. How do I carry it to a machine?
journal.strataindustria.t5.cable.note: Copper in rubber, laid block to block. The power follows it.
journal.strataindustria.t5.cinnabar.hint: Cinnabar is red as rust and hides in basalt and shale. Only steel will cut it.
journal.strataindustria.t5.cinnabar.lead: A red ore turns up in the dark rock, and it breaks my pick. What is it?
journal.strataindustria.t5.circuit.hint: Fit red alloy wire and redstone to a circuit board. Boards are paper soaked in creosote.
journal.strataindustria.t5.circuit.lead: Wire alone does nothing. What would let a machine decide?
journal.strataindustria.t5.circuit.note: Red wire on a soaked board. The first circuit.
journal.strataindustria.t5.dynamo.hint: Turn a kinetic dynamo at 8 RPM or more. It makes 0.25 J/t for each RPM.
journal.strataindustria.t5.dynamo.lead: Magnet, wire and something turning. Could that make power?
journal.strataindustria.t5.dynamo.note: The dynamo spins and the wire hums. Power from a shaft.
journal.strataindustria.t5.electric_chai: Let an electric machine finish 64 items in a row at full power, fed and emptied by item pipe, with nobody opening it.
I still carry ore from machine to machine. Could the wire and pipes run the whole line?
A line from macerator to furnace to chest, and nobody there to run it.
journal.strataindustria.t5.electric_heat: Put an electric heater under a smelter or against a heat pipe and let it heat something.
A firebox needs fuel and tending. Could the wire heat a crucible instead?
The coil glows and the crucible warms. No fuel to carry.
Feed an electrolyser water. It gives hydrogen and oxygen, one tank each.
Could the wire pull water apart?
Two gases from one water, twice as much hydrogen as oxygen.
journal.strataindustria.t5.first_machine: Connect a machine to a dynamo or battery box with cable and put something in it.
I have power in the wire. What can it do?
The machine woke, worked, and slowed when the shaft did.
journal.strataindustria.t5.item_pipe.hin: Run item pipes from an extractor or an inserter to a chest. Items go to the nearest chest that takes them.
journal.strataindustria.t5.item_pipe.lea: I carry every load by hand. Could pipes do it?
journal.strataindustria.t5.item_pipe.not: Items travel the pipe and land in the chest. No hands.
journal.strataindustria.t5.latex.hint: Jungle trees bleed latex. Plant one at home if the jungle is far; dandelions will do in a pinch.
journal.strataindustria.t5.latex.lead: Some trees run thick and white where the bark is cut. Could I collect it?
journal.strataindustria.t5.latex.note: Latex, slow and sticky. A cup fills in about a day.
journal.strataindustria.t5.lightning.hin: Stand a mast of three or more lightning rods on a Leyden jar bank and wait for a thunderstorm.
journal.strataindustria.t5.lightning.lea: Every storm throws more power at the hill than I make in a week. Could I catch some?
journal.strataindustria.t5.lightning.not: A mast of rods over a row of jars. One bolt filled them.
journal.strataindustria.t5.macerator.hin: Put ore in a macerator. It gives a second piece a quarter of the time.
journal.strataindustria.t5.macerator.lea: The crusher needs a shaft and steam. Could a machine on the wire do its work?
journal.strataindustria.t5.macerator.not: The macerator grinds ore to grit, and often gives me a second piece.
journal.strataindustria.t5.mv.hint: Sneak and right-click a machine with an MV upgrade kit.
journal.strataindustria.t5.mv.lead: My machines are slow. Can they take more power?
journal.strataindustria.t5.mv.note: The same machine runs four times as fast on the heavier supply.
journal.strataindustria.t5.ore_scanner.h: Charge an ore scanner at a battery box, then hold right-click to scan around you.
journal.strataindustria.t5.ore_scanner.l: Prospecting by pick is slow. Could a machine do it for me?
journal.strataindustria.t5.ore_scanner.n: The scanner showed me every ore for three chunks around.
Give a power hammer a recorded pattern, or two ingots and flux to weld. It heats the work itself.
The steam hammer needs a boiler and a heat pipe. Could the hammer heat its own work?
The coil heats the metal and the hammer falls. No firebox needed.
journal.strataindustria.t5.power_line.hi: Serve a machine across 64 blocks of overhead span: poles, insulators and ACSR conductor.
journal.strataindustria.t5.power_line.le: Cable wastes power over distance. Is there a way to carry it far?
journal.strataindustria.t5.power_line.no: Pole to pole across the valley, and the machine at the far end ran.
journal.strataindustria.t5.red_alloy.hin: Melt copper first, then add redstone: about two parts copper to three of redstone.
journal.strataindustria.t5.red_alloy.lea: Redstone carries a signal like nothing else. Could copper carry it further?
journal.strataindustria.t5.red_alloy.not: Copper and redstone ran together into a dull red metal.
journal.strataindustria.t5.rubber.hint: Set latex in a sealed barrel, then roast the raw rubber at 140 °C.
journal.strataindustria.t5.rubber.lead: Latex sets soft and tacky. How do I make it hold its shape?
journal.strataindustria.t5.rubber.note: Roasted slowly, the raw rubber turned firm and springy.
journal.strataindustria.t5.stethoscope.h: Right-click a running machine, cable or gearbox with a stethoscope.
journal.strataindustria.t5.stethoscope.l: The shed hums, but I cannot tell if it is well. Could I hear it?
journal.strataindustria.t5.stethoscope.n: A steady beat is a good machine. A rough one is short of power.
journal.strataindustria.t5.storage.hint: Connect a powered storage controller to four chests set to storage mode.
journal.strataindustria.t5.storage.lead: Chests everywhere and I never know what is in which. Could one screen list them?
journal.strataindustria.t5.storage.note: One screen, every chest. Powered, it also moves items.
journal.strataindustria.t5.sulfuric_acid: Mix sulfur dioxide, oxygen and water in a mixer. Roast sulfur for the gas.
Lye eats grease. Is there something that eats stone and metal?
Acid, heavy and clear. It needs a tank and a steady hand.
journal.strataindustria.t5.transformer.h: Join an LV and an MV network with a transformer and pass power through it.
journal.strataindustria.t5.transformer.l: LV and MV do not mix. Is there a way to pass power between them?
journal.strataindustria.t5.transformer.n: The transformer hums. A little is lost, and both sides stay apart.
journal.strataindustria.t5.turbine.hint: Pipe steam into the back of a steam turbine. At 2 bar it settles at full output after ten seconds.
journal.strataindustria.t5.turbine.lead: A steam engine turns a shaft and a dynamo turns it back. Is there a shorter way?
journal.strataindustria.t5.turbine.note: Steam straight to power, with no shaft between.
journal.strataindustria.t5.wire.hint: Draw copper rods thin on the anvil with a draw plate.
journal.strataindustria.t5.wire.lead: A rod is too thick to carry much. Could I draw it out thinner?
journal.strataindustria.t5.wire.note: Pulled through the plate, the rod became fine wire. Slow work.
journal.strataindustria.ui.no_leads: Nothing to chase yet. Look around.
Iron takes one more blow, steel two more

strataindustria.bloomery.not_iron: Only iron-bearing items go in a bloomery
